title: Singapore's Contribution to Loss and Damage Fund Set Up in COP27
what_it_is: Singapore's Contribution to Loss and Damage Fund Set Up in COP27

sections.label: IPCC report on climate impacts
sections.summary: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report states climate change causes widespread loss and damage, with nearly half the world's population highly vulnerable and small island states like Singapore at risk of submergence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: According to the Sixth Assessment Report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Working Group II, climate change is already causing widespread loss and damage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Close to half of the world's population live in contexts that are highly vulnerable to climate change.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Of note, small island states like Singapore are disproportionately affected by sea level rise and are at risk of submergence by century's end, if nothing is done to prevent it.

sections.label: Transitional Committee fund recommendations
sections.summary: A Transitional Committee is tasked to recommend details of the fund by COP28, considering all stakeholders' views, and Singapore will engage constructively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: A Transitional Committee has been tasked to make recommendations by COP28 on the details of the fund, taking into consideration the views of all stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Singapore will engage constructively with the Transitional Committee.

sections.label: Singapore fund pledge question
sections.summary: The question asks whether Singapore will pledge to the fund, noting Singapore emits 0.1% of global carbon emissions but is affected by 100% of climate impacts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, to rephrase my question, would Singapore be pledging to contribute to the fund, bearing in mind that the details are still being worked out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We emit 0.1% of global carbon emissions, but are affected by 100% of all the impacts of climate change.

sections.label: S$100 billion financial resources
sections.summary: Singapore is dedicating up to an estimated S$100 billion, diverting significant financial resources from other urgent needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In fact, we are dedicating a significant part of financial resources – we estimated up to S$100 billion dollars and that is diverting a lot of financial resources away from other urgent needs.

sections.label: Undiscussed international contribution decision
sections.summary: The understanding is that this has not been discussed internationally, and a decision is needed on whether to contribute to or claim from the fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The understanding is that we have not even had a chance to discuss this internationally and we have to decide whether we will contribute or we will claim from this fund.
